name: Barclays

roles.title: Quantitative Developer (Markets / QA)
roles.notes: Live official posting (JR-0000135313, Prague, Cross Markets): develops 'advanced models and analytics that power trading, risk management, and quantitative strategies' for credit and securitisation; requirements name C++ plus Python, shared-codebase development, financial mathematics, Linux RHEL/Windows and distributed systems (Symphony/Kafka/Redis).

roles.title: Rates Quantitative Analyst (Front-office QA)
roles.notes: Live official posting (JR-0000121569, New York, VP): designs stochastic interest-rate models for pricing and risk of vanilla/exotic derivatives; names curve construction, SABR/ZABR volatility calibration, C++ and Python, and numerical methods.

roles.title: Quantitative Analytics Market Risk Modeler
roles.notes: Role title appears in Barclays' official job search results (search.jobs.barclays) for 'quantitative analyst' (Mumbai); posting content not fetched, so treat the track mapping as inferred.

publishedExpectations.claim: Official Quantitative Developer posting: 'To be successful... you should have: Excellent programming skills in C++ and scripting languages (Python). Experience working in a shared codebase within a multi-developer environment. Willingness to learn financial mathematics...' plus highly valued 'Experience with building cross platform (Linux RHEL/Windows) applications and distributed systems (Symphony/Kafka/Redis)'.

Official Rates Quantitative Analyst. VP posting lists: 'Stochastic interest-rate modeling for options, exotics, and structured rates products', 'Expertise in curve construction, volatility surface calibration and modeling (e.g., SABR/ZABR), and multi-factor short-rate models', 'Programming skills in C++ and Python for quantitative finance applications', and 'Numerical methods, nonlinear analytics, and production-grade library development'.

Both postings state the assessment frame: 'You may be assessed on the key critical skills relevant for this role, such as risk and controls, change and transformation, business acumen, strategic thinking and digital and technology, as well as job-specific technical skills.'

Inferred: interview format details (online tests, technical rounds, timelines) are not published on the job pages themselves; community-reported Barclays numerical/coding screens should be treated as unconfirmed. Learners must consult the official careers hub (https://home.barclays/careers/ and https://search.jobs.barclays/) for the current process.

notes: Barclays publishes unusually concrete skill bars on individual postings (both quoted postings were live in Oct-Nov 2026): the quant-dev seat is C++/Python-first with Linux and distributed-systems exposure valued, and the rates QA seat names stochastic modelling, SABR/ZABR calibration, curve construction and production-grade numerical libraries. The QA role family also carries a firmwide assessment frame (risk and controls, business acumen, digital and technology). What Barclays does not publish: interview format specifics, treat community reports of online tests and multi-round technical interviews as unverified. Job search: https://search.jobs.barclays/.
